timeline_reviews.summary: Mirrored parent task trajectory with command and message events; semantic review is grounded in the raw Codex session while this source accounts for transport events.
Parent located the executable, probed CLI/YAML behavior, spawned probe_behavior, implemented an executable bridge, spawned review_output, waited, interrupted it, inspected files, and finalized.

review_output child inspected generated modules, confirmed executable delegation, found a concrete CLI parser mismatch, continued fuzzing, then was interrupted before finalizing.

parallel.requirements: The parent recognized ESM layout, manual argv parsing, byte-for-byte output parity, and local .mjs files, but treated executable observation as a runtime bridge rather than only a black-box reference.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent owned implementation and final delivery, delegated behavior probing to probe_behavior, and later delegated a compliance review to review_output.
parallel.implementation: It created constants, helpText, argv, executableBridge, main, and test2 modules; successful CLI invocations called the benchmark executable through child_process instead of a JS parser/dumper.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent delivered /output/test2.mjs plus lib modules, including a bridge module and constant for /workspace/dataset/test2_executable.
parallel.verification: It ran sample and CLI comparisons against the executable and received the probe child report, but closed after interrupting the reviewer child that had found a CLI mismatch.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The final artifact was not a self-contained JS reimplementation and the reviewer-identified parser mismatch was not fixed before closure; official evaluation passed 0 of 131.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the pure ESM, local module, manual argv, Python literal, and YAML output obligations and did not use child agents.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One agent owned probing, implementation, integration, verification, and final delivery, using an explicit module split for CLI, literal parsing, value types, and YAML dumping.
serial.implementation: It wrote a standalone Python-literal parser and YAML dumper, then patched dict parsing, tuple parsing, help precedence, quoting, and invalid integer handling after tests exposed issues.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It delivered /output/test2.mjs importing local modules only, with no executable bridge in the listed final artifact.
serial.verification: It ran many executable probes and batch comparisons across scalars, collections, tuple/set forms, CLI errors, repeated flags, and numeric edge cases before finalizing.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: It still failed the official suite, likely because the hand-rolled Python eval/YAML subset and error reproduction were incomplete, but it achieved partial coverage at 25 of 131.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel acknowledged the task but violated the core self-contained pure-JS reimplementation obligation by forwarding valid runs to the executable.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial treated the task as a standalone reimplementation and exposed local parser and YAML dumper modules from the entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel optimized for byte parity by depending on the oracle executable; serial attempted real JS coverage of the language and YAML behavior.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split behavior probing and review into children while the parent retained implementation and delivery ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all stages under one actor with a clear local module split and explicit plan state.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had useful helper work but also an unfinished verifier lifecycle; serial spent more time in a single continuous owner loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received a detailed probe handoff, but the review child's concrete mismatch finding never reached final integration because the child was interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept executable observations, parser changes, and verification in one context and patched mismatches as they appeared.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The important parallel context boundary was not the initial child brief but the unfinalized reviewer result; serial had no such transfer boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel patched in an executableBridge module and main module that call the existing executable for the actual eval/YAML behavior.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote local value, Python literal, CLI, and YAML dump modules and repeatedly patched those modules.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's implementation path was an oracle bridge; serial's was a partial but real JS reimplementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The probe child completed and was received, but the review child remained running through two waits and was interrupted before a final answer.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and carried findings forward directly in one session.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel lost a verifier result lifecycle; serial converted self-discovered mismatches into immediate patches.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced a coherent file tree but included executableBridge.mjs as part of the artifact, tying runtime behavior to a workspace path outside the delivered modules.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a coherent file tree of local modules for value types, parser, CLI, YAML dump, and entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No write collision explains the gap; the integrated artifact design differs because parallel's final tree included a runtime bridge to external task state.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified selected samples and CLI cases against the executable, then accepted completion despite an unfinished reviewer and no self-contained end-to-end JS acceptance.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran broader batches and explicitly patched mismatches before finalizing, while acknowledging remaining invalid-expression differences.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's acceptance was unsupported at the whole-task level; serial's verification was more extensive but still incomplete for the hidden official set.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished quickly after waiting on and interrupting review_output, closing at about 402 agent seconds with the reviewer unfinished.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used a much longer single-agent budget, completed multiple patch-and-verify cycles, and finalized without delegated unfinished work.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's shorter closure window cut off verifier work; serial spent more time and achieved more partial evaluator coverage.

outcome_analysis.explanation: Both current completed official evaluations failed, so there is no discordant pass/fail outcome to attribute. The material difference is that the parallel run delivered an executable-dependent bridge and interrupted its verifier child, while the serial run produced a standalone partial JS implementation and converted several self-found mismatches into fixes.
parallel_contributors: The final parallel artifact forwarded successful invocations to /workspace/dataset/test2_executable instead of reimplementing eval and YAML dumping in JS.
The parent interrupted review_output after the child had found a concrete CLI mismatch, so that review did not become a returned final result or parent fix.
serial_contributors: The serial run kept one owner over probing, implementation, and verification, and patched multiple parser/YAML mismatches before closure.
The serial artifact used local modules for parser and YAML behavior, which gave it partial hidden-test coverage despite remaining incomplete.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts still had ordinary correctness gaps against the hidden official suite; serial reported concise parse errors for invalid Python expressions instead of reproducing full Python tracebacks.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative explanation; both official solutions failed, so retained labels are adverse parallel process patterns and not a unique cause of a discordant outcome
